label: Gatterer 1767 distinguishes source-grounded and presentational routes to historical Evidenz
subject: work.gatterer-von-der-evidenz-geschichtskunde.1767
object: vivid presentational production of spectator-like conviction

sources.citation: Johann Christoph Gatterer, Vorrede von der Evidenz in der Geschichtskunde, in Friedrich Eberhard Boysen (ed.), Die allgemeine Welthistorie, vol. 1 (Halle: Gebauer, 1767), pp. 1-38
Daniel Fulda and subsequent scholarship on Gatterer's 1767 Evidenz theory, source demonstration and vivid spectator-like narration

observations.value: Historical factuality can be warranted by exposing the principles/sources on which the account rests.
Historical narration can generate Evidenz by becoming so lebhaft and anschauend that the reader becomes, as it were, a Zuschauer.
The two routes can be combined but should not be collapsed: presentational force is not identical to source warrant.

claim_limit: This distinction and Gatterer's vividness theory are established historiographical prior art. The project-specific question is how colour/colour-surrogates occupy and move between these routes across concrete practices.

label: Working colour-method hinge: chromatic Evidenz does not inherit historical warrant automatically

observations.value: A colour, hatch or illuminated table may increase perceptual Evidenz, inspection speed or mnemonic force without independently increasing the source/system warrant of the relation it displays.
low relational warrant + high chromatic/perceptual Evidenz can produce apparent certainty
For every colour operation, record separately the warrant for the underlying historical category/relation and the perceptual work performed by the chromatic carrier.

sources.citation: Modern scholarship on Gatterer's source-grounded and presentational Evidenz

claim_limit: Do not imply that Gatterer himself explicitly theorized pigment as a separate Evidenz category in 1767; the colour application is a project inference to test against later tables, heraldry and copy evidence.
